page: Amazon Web Services c8g.medium is an entry-level compute-optimized virtual instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AWS Graviton4 processors. It provides 1 dedicated physical core mapped to 1 vCPU based on the 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.8 GHz. The processor includes hardware AES cryptographic support alongside 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory allocation is configured at 2.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a compute-aligned 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. This instance includes no bundled local storage, relying on network-attached volumes, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps with no complimentary public IPv4 addresses and zero hardware accelerators.

Benchmark data displays solid single-threaded performance in specific computational routines paired with expected constraints of a single-core instance. In single-threaded compression and decompression, the instance demonstrates capable execution, reaching 14.02 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression and 30.01 GB/sec in gzip compression, alongside an average single-core stress-ng score of 1693.68. Conversely, overall throughput in multi-core metrics, PassMark aggregates, and memory streaming tests ranks in the bottom quartiles, such as 30.05 GB/sec uncached large-block reads and 11.61 GB/sec large-block writes. Application workloads reveal 2.38 million Redis SET operations per second and 2.34 GB/sec of static web serving throughput.

The primary operational tradeoff of the c8g.medium is its limited single-core footprint and modest 2.0 GB memory envelope, which limits concurrency and large in-memory footprints. However, its modern Neoverse-V2 core delivers stable instruction execution for low-intensity continuous background processing. The instance serves cost-efficiently as an execution environment for lightweight microservices, single-threaded batch automation, small build agents, CI/CD runners, and edge utility scripts requiring ARM64 execution.
description: Amazon Web Services c8g.medium is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro system and the AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 Graviton4 platform. It features 1 dedicated vCPU operating at 2.8 GHz, 2.0 GB of system memory, and 1 Gbps of baseline networking bandwidth. The instance includes 36 MB of L3 cache and hardware AES encryption, but provides no integrated local storage or GPU hardware. In synthetic benchmarks, single-threaded tasks show efficient execution, recording 14.02 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression and steady gzip throughput, whereas aggregate system scores and memory bandwidth reflect its single-threaded ceiling. With low resource overhead and dedicated core sizing, c8g.medium functions as an economical computing node for small ARM64 microservices, lightweight web servers, routine script automation, and continuous integration worker tasks.
